messages:
sam: anyone seeing intermittent east-west packet loss in us-west2 GPU cluster when autoscaler starts backfills? only seeing it between hosts on overlay (vxlan). pods time out, not all traffic.

taylor: yup saw a blip earlier. looks like only encapsulated traffic. host NICs fine. suspect MTU/offload mismatch + rapid pod churn. :thinking:

kai: can you paste a tcpdump or ip -s link? curious if packets are being dropped before encap or after.

sam: quick tcpdump from host-A toward host-B: \n```
12:01:11.123456 IP host-A > host-B: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
12:01:11.123497 IP host-A > host-B: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 (retransmit)
12:01:11.223900 IP host-A > host-B: ICMP frag needed, mtu 1420
```

sam: also `ip link show vxlan0` shows MTU 1450 on some nodes and 1500 on others (weird): `vxlan0@vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN` on host-A, host-B has 1500.

taylor: that MTU mismatch is classic. also check sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing and net.ipv4.ip_forward. I've seen iptables MASQUERADE on certain nodes that rewrites path and triggers DF/ICMP blackhole.

mike: fyi RDMA flows (roce) seemed mostly ok but saw this in dmesg on host-C: `mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: firmware error: RAQ overflow` - could be unrelated but coincident with the window.

kai: can we rule out GRO/GSO? run: `ethtool -k eth0 | egrep "gso|gro|tso"` and `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_mtu_probing`.

sam: ran on host-A: `gso: on\ngro: on\ntso: on` and tcp_mtu_probing=0. host-B had gro off, mtu 1500.

taylor: mixed offloads + MTU mismatch + encapsulation = fragmented packets dropped. quick mitigation: enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 on workers or set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=2 per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1191. also consider aligning vxlan MTU and force GSO/GRO off on vxlan interface until kernel patch.

ops-bot: incident.alert: 3 pods in us-west2-gpu reported network-timeout in the last 10m. severity: medium. link: https://ops/redwood/incidents/4521 :ambulance:

kai: small test suggestion - run `tracepath -n <peer>` from both hosts. if you see MTU drop to 1420 and no ICMP return, we have a blackhole. also try `mtudisc-test` or send small/large pings with DF set.

mike: captured a pcap on host-B showing ENCAP out then nothing at underlay egress for some frames. snippet: `VXLAN(udp) -> outer len 1500 but inner payload 1600 -> fragment needed`. seems fragmentation isn't handled because of offload.

sam: proposed immediate actions: \n- set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on us-west2 workers (staging first)\n- align vxlan MTU to 1450 via CNI config and roll canary nodes\n- temporarily disable GRO on vxlan interfaces on 4 suspect hosts (`ethtool -K vxlan0 gro off gso off tso off`)\n- pause autoscaler backfills for 30m while we test

taylor: I'm gonna push sysctl to staging canary now. will monitor metrics (retransmit %, pod restarts). tagging @mike for RDMA log correlation.

kai: I'll run tracepath and collect tcpdump on a pair of nodes during a controlled backfill. dropping pcap to /tmp/vxlan-loss-1729.pcap

mike: I'll grep dmesg for mlx5/errors and check HCA counters. if we see firmware errors + encapsulation drops we may need a NIC microcode update.

sam: thanks. if anyone hits this live please react here with `!drop` and include hostnames. we should schedule a quick oncall huddle if mitigation fails. :thumbsup:

taylor: update 15m: staging canary shows no retransmits after tcp_mtu_probing=1 and vxlan MTU aligned. still validating under load.

sam: ok will hold autoscaler for 30m on us-west2-gpu. follow-up to eng-sre to track NIC microcode rollout and CNI MTU enforcement.

mike: note for postmortem: autoscaler launch pattern created a burst of encapsulated flows that exposed inconsistent host config - need preflight checks in node bootstrap (mtu+offloads+kmod versions).

sam: action items recorded. kai/taylor/mike to update thread with artifacts (pcap, ethtool outputs, tracepath). closing for now unless we see more alerts.
